cases.name: grouping-key-collision-stale-upstream-cache
cases.boundary: OCaml rebuilds roles after joined-key collision removal; Go removes the caller tuple from the role cache and leaves the removed stored tuple active.

cases.name: strict-policy-arity-two-fields
cases.boundary: OCaml rejects wrong-arity p operations atomically; Go stores the short row, exposes it in queries, and fails later enforcement until it is removed.

cases.name: strict-policy-arity-four-fields
cases.boundary: OCaml rejects oversized p rules before mutation; Go stores them and reports an enforcement size error.

cases.name: strict-grouping-short-row
cases.boundary: Go returns an error for a short g add but leaves the malformed row stored until removal; OCaml rejects before mutation. Wrong-arity query/remove calls are also rejected by OCaml.

cases.name: strict-grouping-extra-field
cases.boundary: OCaml requires exactly two grouping fields. Go stores extra fields but builds a role link using only the first two.

cases.name: strict-grouping-cycle-preserves-state
cases.boundary: Raw Go grouping mutations accept cycles. OCaml validates the candidate graph and retains the previous snapshot on rejection.

cases.name: strict-self-edge-preserves-state
cases.boundary: OCaml rejects explicit self edges while preserving implicit self membership. Raw Go mutations store the edge.

cases.name: duplicate-before-self-cycle-validation
cases.note: The comma-key identity already exists under a distinct valid tuple. Adding a key-colliding self tuple is a no-op, so graph validation must occur only after the duplicate check.
